bull.b: The sharp FY2026 revenue increase and return to very high profitability demonstrate strong operating leverage during the current recovery. If elevated demand and improved product mix persist, the resulting earnings base can support reinvestment, technology development, and stronger competitive positioning.

Multi-year New Business Models provide materially greater revenue visibility than spot NAND sales and deepen relationships with Datacenter and Edge customers. Their growing share of bits could reduce dependence on short-term volume decisions while supporting product planning and capacity utilization.

Strong conversion of earnings into operating and free cash flow gives SanDisk substantial internal funding for capacity, product ramps, and capital returns. Combined with very low leverage, this provides financial flexibility to withstand industry swings and pursue strategic priorities without heavy debt dependence.

bear.b: The magnitude of the recent earnings rebound also highlights the business’s exposure to NAND pricing, demand, and production cycles. Prior losses and negative free cash flow show that exceptional current results may not be durable across a full cycle, creating meaningful uncertainty for medium-term earnings stability.

Consumer weakness remains a direct pressure on a business that historically sells branded removable media and storage into electronics markets. Although full-year consumer revenue grew, the quarterly decline and delayed recovery expectation could constrain volumes and mix while Datacenter growth continues to scale.

Persistent allocation indicates SanDisk may be unable to satisfy all incremental demand, limiting near-term revenue capture even in a favorable market. At the same time, greater reliance on large NBM customers concentrates execution and relationship risk, making a few contracts more important to future results.
